findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, so the feature flag check is dead logic
findings.body: The helper reads FlagSqlExpressions, then returns false on both branches of `if enabled`. The flag value has no effect, so the SQL case always returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. The name suggests flag-driven enablement, which misleads anyone who later wants to re-enable SQL expressions by flag. They would have to rewrite the helper, and the flag lookup is still evaluated on the SQL path, which the previous code did not do. If h.features is ever nil, this now panics for SQL queries where it previously did not. Replace the helper with an unconditional rejection, or keep the flag check and drop the forced false.

findings.title: Existing SQL expression parsing and execution tests will fail, and no test covers the new rejection
findings.body: TablesList now always fails because DB.RunCommands in db.go always returns an error, so NewSQLCommand also always fails. Any existing test expecting TablesList or NewSQLCommand to return table names, or expecting SQL command execution to produce frames, will now fail. The PR does not touch any test files. Nothing in the diff asserts that a SQL query is rejected at ReadQuery (reader.go, SQL case), or that the stub DB returns errors. Either the affected tests are left broken, or the PR is missing coverage for the new behavior. Update or remove the old SQL tests and add a test for the rejection path.

findings.title: UnmarshalSQLCommand bypasses the ExpressionQueryReader gate
findings.body: The new check lives only in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery. UnmarshalSQLCommand is exported and calls NewSQLCommand directly with no feature or enable check. Right now SQL execution is blocked only because the stub DB returns errors. If a real engine is reintroduced in pkg/expr/sql/db.go, this path would reach it without the gate. Put the guard in NewSQLCommand or UnmarshalSQLCommand too, so the protection does not depend on a single call path.

findings.title: Nil pointer dereference when building the unloading threshold fails (pre-existing)
findings.body: This is not introduced by the PR, but it is in the same file. `unloading, err := NewThresholdCommand(...)` is followed by `unloading.Invert = true` before the `if err != nil` check on the next line. If NewThresholdCommand returns a nil pointer on error, a user-supplied invalid unloadCondition evaluator type causes a panic while parsing the query. Move the error check above the field assignment.
